title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21|

   30| ```

sys.path.insert(0, REPO)
from TokenCore import TokenCore  # authors' code, unmodified

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", None)


def load_grammar():
    data = np.load(os.path.join(REPO, "data", "grammar.npy"), allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = data["tokens"]                      # list of word lists
    labels = [[int(x) for x in l] for l in data["labels"]]  # JSON uses '0'/'1' strings; npy uses ints -> normalize to int
    doc_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]       # R11
    # cross-check against the JSON annotation document labels
    js = json.load(open(os.path.join(REPO, "data", "grammar_correction_labeled.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
    js_labels = {str(x["data"]["text"]).strip(): int(x["data"]["label"]) for x in js}
    mism = sum(1 for t, dl in zip(data["sentences"], doc_labels)
               if js_labels.get(str(t).strip(), dl) != dl)

    assert n_anom == 30 and len(tokens) - n_anom == 270, "R10 violated"
    assert mism == 0, f"{mism} doc-label mismatches vs JSON"
    return tokens, labels, doc_labels

    """50% of normal docs for training; rest + all anomalous for testing (R6)."""

    anom_idx = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 1])

    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(name, **kw).eval()

# Reproduction of "Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection" (TokenCore)
# Target claim C1: token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset (Table 1).
# Pipeline: 50% of normal docs -> memory bank; BERT-base-uncased;
# element-wise max pooling over subwords via the AUTHORS' align.py
# extract_word_embeddings (Eq.1); nearest-neighbor L2 token score via the
# AUTHORS' TokenCore.py (Eq.2); mean aggregation for document score (Eq.3).
import argparse, contextlib, io, json, os, sys, time
import numpy as np

REPO = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo")
sys.path.insert(0, REPO)
from TokenCore import TokenCore                          # authors' code, unmodified
from align import extract_word_embeddings                # authors' code, unmodified

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", None)


def load_grammar():
    data = np.load(os.path.join(REPO, "data", "grammar.npy"), allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = data["tokens"]                                  # list of word lists
    labels = [[int(x) for x in l] for l in data["labels"]]   # normalize '0'/'1' -> int
    doc_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]        # R11
    js = json.load(open(os.path.join(REPO, "data", "grammar_correction_labeled.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
    js_labels = {str(x["data"]["text"]).strip(): int(x["data"]["label"]) for x in js}
    mism = sum(1 for t, dl in zip(data["sentences"], doc_labels)
               if js_labels.get(str(t).strip(), dl) != dl)
    assert len(tokens) == 300, f"expected 300 docs, got {len(tokens)}"
    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    assert n_anom == 30 and len(tokens) - n_anom == 270, "R10 violated"
    assert mism == 0, f"{mism} doc-label mismatches vs JSON"
    return tokens, labels, doc_labels


def split_docs(doc_labels, seed):
    """50% of normal docs for training; rest + all anomalous for testing (R6)."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    normal_idx = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 0])
    anom_idx = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 1])
    perm = rng.permutation(len(normal_idx))
    half = len(normal_idx) // 2
    return normal_idx[perm[:half]], np.concatenate([normal_idx[perm[half:]], anom_idx])


def embed_words_authors(tokens_list, backbone="bert-base-uncased"):

def spot_check(embs, tokens, labels, doc_labels, seed, n_docs=3):
    """Print gold word units of anomalous sentences with their per-token score and
    the nearest memory-bank word, to confirm positives are genuinely corrupted
    words (not an alignment offset artefact)."""
    train_idx, test_idx = split_docs(doc_labels, seed)
    X_train = np.concatenate([embs[i] for i in train_idx], axis=0)
    bank_words = [w for i in train_idx for w in tokens[i]]
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=1)
    model.fit(X_train)
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    out = []
    anom_test = [i for i in test_idx if doc_labels[i] == 1][:n_docs]
    for i in anom_test:
        dist, idx = model.nbrs.kneighbors(embs[i])
        toks = []
        for j, w in enumerate(tokens[i]):
            toks.append({"word": w, "gold_label": labels[i][j],
                         "score": round(float(dist[j, 0]), 3),
                         "nn_word": bank_words[int(idx[j, 0])]})
        out.append({"doc_id": int(i), "sentence": " ".join(tokens[i]),
                    "gold_positive_words": [w for w, l in zip(tokens[i], labels[i]) if l == 1],

        print(f"\nSPOT CHECK doc {i}: {out[-1]['sentence']}")
        print(f"  gold positives: {out[-1]['gold_positive_words']}")

            print(f"  {t['word']:<15} score={t['score']:<8} nn='{t['nn_word']}'{mark}")

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The reproduction is methodologically faithful for C1: it runs the authors' TokenCore.py and align.py on the full 300-document Grammar benchmark, builds a normal-doc-only memory bank from 135 training documents, scores test tokens by 1-NN L2 distance, and aggregates documents by mean. The clean rerun exits 0 in about 40 s and gives token AUROC 0.5978 at seed 0, a 5-seed mean of 0.5723±0.0158, token AUPRC 0.0346 and document AUROC 0.5121; the paper's C1 value 0.6371 is therefore not within the ±0.02 band. The gap is plausibly due to paper underspecification rather than wrong data or cheating: the split seed is unreleased (A12), the embedding layer/normalization is unspecified (A13), and the token-level pooling protocol is unspecified (A14); a logged last-4-layer mean plus L2-normalization variant reaches 0.6631 at seed 0, bracketing the paper value. Spot checks confirm the 47 gold positives are genuine grammar-error tokens, not alignment artefacts. Only TokenCore is run, so the six baseline comparisons (R8) are missing and broader ranking claims are not audited, but C1's dataset, metric and proposed method are correct.
